entry.title: EWM Outbound: The Correct Sequence for Correcting a Delivery Item After Warehouse Task Confirmation
entry.content:
Introduction
One of the most common process mistakes in SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) outbound operations happens when a warehouse coordinator or logistics analyst needs to correct a delivery item,  a quantity change, a batch reassignment, or a batch split sub-item removal after the warehouse task has already been confirmed and the stock is packed into a Handling Unit (HU).

The instinct is to go directly to the ERP delivery (VL02N) and make the correction. It seems logical: the issue is in the delivery document, so fix the delivery document. However, this approach, while intuitive, breaks the reference link between the EWM HU and the ERP delivery item, causing a silent but severe data inconsistency that only surfaces when the system tries to proceed to the next step in the outbound process.

This post documents the problem pattern, explains why it happens, and provides the correct step-by-step sequence to follow whenever a delivery item correction is needed after picking has been confirmed.

The Problem — What Goes Wrong

Symptoms

When the wrong sequence is followed, the following symptoms appear in EWM:

  • Warehouse request is empty — no items available to generate new warehouse tasks
  • Physical stock in the HU shows Item = 0 — the HU contains stock but references a delivery item that no longer exists
  • Subsequent warehouse task cannot be created — the outbound flow to staging or GI zone is blocked
  • Goods Issue cannot be posted — the entire outbound billing chain is halted

The Root Cause

In SAP EWM, when a warehouse task is confirmed, the system creates a direct link between the physical stock in the Handling Unit and the delivery item in the EWM Outbound Delivery Order (ODO). This link is stored at the HU item level with a reference to the specific delivery item number.

When the delivery item is then modified or deleted in ERP — for example, by removing a Batch Split (BSP) sub-item or zeroing out the main item quantity — EWM is not aware of this change until a full redistribution of the delivery occurs. In the meantime, the HU item still holds the old reference. If that delivery item no longer exists, the reference becomes orphaned, and the field Item in the HU physical stock view shows 0 (zero), meaning: "this stock is assigned to this delivery, but to an item that no longer exists."

The result:

HU has stock → delivery item reference = 0 (orphaned)
Warehouse request → empty (no valid items to pick)
Next step (YEST / GI zone) → cannot be triggered
Goods Issue → blocked

How to Identify the Issue

Before attempting any correction, confirm the inconsistency:

Step 1 — Check the Warehouse Request

  • Run the warehouse task creation transaction for the affected ODO
  • If the "Solic. depósito" (Warehouse Request) tab is empty → issue confirmed

Step 2 — Check Physical Stock (/SCWM/ADHU)

  1. Run /SCWM/ADHU
  2. Search by Warehouse Number and Document (ODO number)
  3. Open the Physical Stock (Estoque físico) tab
  4. Look for entries where Item = 0 → orphaned HU item confirmed

Step 3 — Trace the Sequence (/SCWM/ACTLOG)

  1. Run /SCWM/ACTLOG
  2. Filter by Warehouse Number and ODO number
  3. Look for a delivery modification that occurred after a warehouse task confirmation
  4. This confirms the wrong sequence was followed

The Wrong Sequence ❌

1. WT confirmed (picking done, stock in HU)     ✓
2. Delivery modified in ERP (VL02N)             ← WRONG — HU not unpacked first
3. Item deleted / quantity zeroed out           ← HU now references non-existing item
4. Item = 0 appears in HU physical stock        ← Inconsistency created
5. Subsequent WT creation fails                 ← Process blocked

The Correct Sequence ✅

Whenever a delivery item needs to be corrected after a warehouse task has been confirmed and stock is packed in an HU, always follow this sequence:

Step 1 — Cancel / Reverse the Warehouse Task Confirmation

  • Navigate to the confirmed warehouse task in EWM
  • Reverse/cancel the confirmation to return stock to its source bin
  • The HU assignment is released

Step 2 — Unpack / Deassign the HU Item

  1. Run /SCWM/ADHU
  2. Locate the HU containing the stock for the affected item
  3. Remove (deassign) the item from the HU
  4. Confirm the physical stock no longer shows the delivery item reference

Step 3 — Perform the Delivery Correction in ERP

  • Run VL02N in ERP
  • Apply the necessary correction (delete BSP sub-item, change batch, adjust quantity, etc.)
  • Save the delivery

Step 4 — Re-distribute the Delivery to EWM

  • Re-save the delivery or use VL06O to push the updated delivery to EWM
  • Confirm the ODO in EWM reflects the corrected items

Step 5 — Re-generate and Execute the Warehouse Task

  • Create a new warehouse task for the corrected items
  • Confirm the task via /SCWM/RFUI or the appropriate RF transaction
  • Pack stock into the HU again
  • Continue the outbound flow normally

Visual Summary

✅ CORRECT SEQUENCE

WT Confirmed → Stock in HU
        ↓
[1] Reverse WT confirmation
        ↓
[2] Unpack HU item (/SCWM/ADHU)
        ↓
[3] Modify delivery in ERP (VL02N)
        ↓
[4] Re-distribute to EWM (VL06O)
        ↓
[5] Re-generate WT → confirm → pack → continue flow

Why This Matters — Business Impact

Skipping steps 1 and 2 before modifying the delivery may seem like a time-saving shortcut, but the consequences are severe:

Impact Area Consequence
Warehouse OperationsPicking tasks cannot be created — pickers are blocked
Outbound LogisticsGoods Issue cannot be posted
Customer BillingInvoice generation delayed or blocked
Data IntegrityOrphaned HU items require manual correction by support team
System RecoveryEach affected ODO requires individual manual data fix

In large warehouse environments with high-volume outbound processing, a single incorrect sequence applied to multiple deliveries can result in significant operational disruption and financial exposure.

Prevention — Process and Authorization Controls

Process Training

Warehouse supervisors and logistics coordinators should be trained on this sequence. A simple rule to communicate to the team:

"Never modify a delivery in ERP if the stock has already been confirmed and packed in EWM. Always unpack and reverse first."

Authorization Control (Recommended)

Consider restricting the user role authorization in ERP to prevent deletion or modification of delivery items that have active HU assignments in EWM. This removes the possibility of the wrong sequence being followed unintentionally.

Proactive Monitoring

Implement a daily check in /SCWM/MON for ODOs that:

  • Have HUs assigned
  • Have no open warehouse tasks
  • Have not yet posted Goods Issue

Catching these early (before the shipping window) avoids escalation to a business-down situation. Moreover, this proactive monitoring should be performed only when the behavior is already noticed but not fixed or identified how many deliveries could be affected by this behavior. 

Conclusion

The EWM outbound process enforces a tight coupling between delivery items in ERP and physical stock in Handling Units. This design ensures data consistency but requires discipline when corrections are needed mid-process. The correct sequence — reverse → unpack → correct → redistribute → re-execute — must always be followed when modifying a delivery item after warehouse task confirmation.

Understanding this sequence is fundamental for anyone operating or supporting EWM outbound processing, and implementing the appropriate process controls prevents it from becoming a recurring incident.

 Author: Jacson Folmer Dias — EWM Consultant | SAP Global Delivery Hub Americas LAC

entry.title: How to do achieve auto Nested packing in EWM
entry.content:
In SAP EWM, a Handling Unit (HU) is a physical unit that combines packaging material and the products packed inside it. Nested Handling Units allow us to create a hierarchy of packaging, where one HU is packed inside another HU.

For example, individual products can be packed into cartons, multiple cartons can be placed on a pallet, and multiple pallets can be loaded onto a truck or another transport unit, depending on the warehouse process.

The main advantage is that EWM can manage the packaging hierarchy and the stock contained within it. Instead of handling every individual carton separately, warehouse operators can move, scan, pick, and track a larger packaging unit while retaining visibility into its contents.

Auto nested packing lets SAP EWM build a full packing hierarchy, such as bottles in cartons and cartons on a pallet, the moment an inbound delivery is created. Warehouse Operator does have to pack manually in EWM, and the system creates every handling unit (HU) for us.

This post uses a simple example. We pack 12 bottles of bottles into one carton, then 5 cartons onto one pallet:

  • 1 carton = 12 bottles
  • 1 pallet = 5 cartons = 60 bottles

Configuration:

  1. Packaging Specifications.

 

1.1 Define the number range for packaging specifications.

 

1.2 Define general packaging specification parameters.

1.3 Define the packaging specification group.

1.4 Maintain the master data for packaging specifications. The level set it uses is defined in step 2.3.

2. Maintain the structure of the packaging specification:

2.1 Define level types. Here you define the packing elements, such as pallet and carton. Set both to HU, so each generates its own HU number and is packed into the other.

2.2 Define element types. Assign a type to each element above. The packing materials act as main or auxiliary packing material.

2.3 Define the level set. Combine all packaging elements and mark whether each one is a packing material. Set the sequence: carton first, then pallet. Assign each level to the main packing element type.

 

 

 

2.4 Define packaging material types.

2.5 Assign the packaging material type to the element type.

3. Determine packaging specifications. Create the determination procedure if you need it.

4. Assign the procedure to the document type, here the inbound delivery document type, so the system looks for a specification when a delivery is created.

 

 

 

5. Master Data

Create the packaging specification for your product

Create the specification itself in transaction /SCWM/PACKSPEC.

1. Create the packaging specification and its condition record for the product. Enter a description and select the packaging specification group.

2. Open the detail view and create the conditions by selecting the condition type.

3. Set up the carton level. Double-click the carton, enter a target quantity of 12 and select HU Creation. The system then creates a HU for the carton as well as for the packing material.

4. Set up the pallet level the same way. Target quantity is 5, because each pallet holds 5 cartons (60 bottles). HU Creation makes the system create a HU for the pallet after the carton.

5. Add the product to the content. Right-click Content and add the product. Open the content, click the product and enter a quantity of 1.

6. Activate and save the specification.

 

The result in the inbound delivery

Create an inbound delivery for 60 bottles. If packing does not come from ECC, EWM packs automatically using the specification. It creates 6 HUs: 5 cartons and 1 pallet, with the 60 bottles in the 5 cartons and the 5 cartons on the pallet.

 

The delivery shows the highest level, the pallet. To see the full structure, select Display HU, which lists the pallet and the cartons packed into it.

Conclusion

Nested Handling Units provide a structured way to manage multiple levels of packaging in SAP EWM. We can pack individual products into cartons, consolidate those cartons onto a pallet, and maintain visibility of the entire packaging hierarchy.

From an operational perspective, this can reduce repetitive scanning and handling, simplify pallet movements, improve packing accuracy, and support better visibility during staging, loading, and shipping.

The key benefit is that we can manage the physical movement of a larger unit without losing track of the smaller units and products packed inside it.

entry.title: Warehouse Process Type Determination for PMR in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud
entry.content:
Warehouse Process Type Determination for PMR in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud

Introduction

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Public Edition, warehouse process configuration plays an important role in ensuring the smooth movement of materials from the warehouse to Production Supply Areas (PSAs). In scenarios involving Scope Item 6NI – Production Supply with Kanban or Advanced Production Integration, the system uses Production Material Requests (PMRs) to support production supply processes.

While working with PMRs, you may notice an interesting behavior: the system automatically determines Warehouse Process Type (WPT) S220 for PMR items, even when no corresponding entry is visible in the standard Determine Warehouse Process Types configuration activity.

This raises a common question: How does SAP determine the warehouse process type when no visible configuration entry exists?

In this blog, we will explore this behavior, explain the role of SAP-delivered configuration, and clarify how the Assign Bin to PSA app influences warehouse task creation.

Details

  1. Understanding the scenario

In the Assign Bin to PSA app (App ID: /SCWM/PSASTAGE), users can maintain bin assignments for Production Supply Areas. These assignments support the staging of materials required for production.

For each material and PSA combination, you may expect the Warehouse Process Type to be determined based on the master data setup.

However, when you check the Determine Warehouse Process Types configuration activity, you may not find a visible entry specifically for PMR documents. Despite this, the system consistently determines WPT S220 for PMR items.

  1. The role of pre-delivered configuration

The behavior is associated with SAP-delivered configuration provided when Scope Item 6NI is activated.

According to this scenario, the system contains preconfigured entries for the following combination:

  • Document Type: PMRC
  • Item Type: PCC
  • Warehouse Process Type: S220

These entries are not visible in the standard configuration UI, but they support the standard PMR process.

As a result, the system automatically determines WPT S220 for PMR items without requiring users to manually maintain a corresponding entry in the configuration activity.

  1. How WPT determination works

The process can be understood in two parts:

Step 1: Default WPT determination

For PMR documents with document type PMRC and item type PCC, the system uses the pre-delivered configuration to determine WPT S220 by default.

Step 2: Staging warehouse task creation

During PSA staging task creation, the system also refers to the settings maintained in the Assign Bin to PSA app. These settings play a role in determining the picking warehouse process type used for the task.

If no applicable custom configuration changes the standard behavior, S220 is used as the default.

This approach supports consistent warehouse process determination while reducing the need for additional manual configuration in standard production supply scenarios.

  1. What should you consider during implementation?

When configuring production supply in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, keep the following points in mind:

  • Understand the standard behavior: S220 is the default WPT for the PMRC/PCC combination in the described scenario.
  • Review PSA bin assignments: Check the Assign Bin to PSA app when validating picking task creation and warehouse process type behavior.
  • Avoid unnecessary configuration: Additional entries may not be required if the standard SAP-delivered behavior meets the business requirement.
  • Validate custom requirements: If the business process requires a different WPT, investigate the available configuration options and their effect on task creation before making changes.

Understanding this behavior can save troubleshooting time when the system determines a WPT even though no corresponding entry is visible in the configuration UI.

Conclusion

When a warehouse process type is determined automatically in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, the absence of a visible configuration entry does not necessarily mean that the system lacks the configuration needed to support the process.

Warehouse Process Type determination for PMRs in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Public Edition, Scope Item 6NI, demonstrates how SAP-delivered configuration supports standard production supply processes.

The key takeaways are:

  • SAP provides pre-delivered configuration for the PMRC document type and PCC item type combination.
  • WPT S220 is the default in the scenario described.
  • The corresponding configuration entries may not be visible in the standard Determine Warehouse Process Types activity.
  • The Assign Bin to PSA app remains relevant when determining the picking WPT during warehouse task creation.
  • Manual configuration should be considered only when the standard behavior does not meet the required business process.

By understanding the relationship between PMR document types, item types, default WPT determination, and PSA bin assignments, SAP EWM consultants can troubleshoot production supply scenarios more effectively and avoid unnecessary configuration changes.
